Clarifying a Misunderstanding in German: B2 Practice

Clarify the intended meaning of your earlier statement in German. Practise gemeint, missverständlich and klarstellen with translations and explained B2 answers.

B2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions + writing task

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Try the exercisesWrite your own sentence

Useful phrases and patterns

A clarification can acknowledge unclear wording and state the intended scope: Meine Formulierung war offenbar missverständlich. Gemeint war nur … explains the intended meaning. Ich beziehe mich auf … identifies the reference, and Ich möchte klarstellen, dass … introduces an explicit clarification.

Common mistake to avoid

Missverständlich describes wording that can be misunderstood; it does not by itself blame the listener. Clarify the actual point rather than assuming an unverified intention.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Notice what the speaker wants to do, the level of politeness and the details the listener needs.

Worked example 1Meine Formulierung war offenbar missverständlich.My wording was evidently open to misunderstanding.
Worked example 2Gemeint war nur der erste Abschnitt, nicht der gesamte Bericht.I meant only the first section, not the whole report.
Worked example 3Ich beziehe mich dabei auf die ursprüngliche Frage.In saying that I am referring to the original question.
Worked example 4Ich möchte klarstellen, dass die Rückmeldung noch vorläufig ist.I would like to clarify that the feedback is still provisional.

Practice: complete the phrases

Complete the clarification using the participle, adjective or infinitive specified by the cue. Use each word-bank item once. Try each question before opening the answer. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Word bank: beziehen · gemeint · klarstellen · missverständlich

Question 1. Damit war ausschließlich der Entwurf ___. (meant)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: gemeint

Gemeint identifies the intended reference.

Question 2. Der Satz war an dieser Stelle ___. (open to misunderstanding)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: missverständlich

Missverständlich acknowledges the unclear wording.

Question 3. Ich möchte mich auf die ursprüngliche Angabe ___. (refer)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: beziehen

Sich beziehen auf identifies the reference; mich is already supplied.

Question 4. Ich möchte ___, dass es um einen Vorschlag geht. (clarify)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: klarstellen

Klarstellen introduces the explicit clarification.

Use it in your own sentence

Clarify that your comment concerned a draft rather than a final report.

Try writing your answer before reading the model below. Other natural answers are possible.

One possible answer

Meine Bemerkung bezog sich auf den Entwurf, nicht auf den fertigen Bericht.

Check your wording: Identify the intended reference so the misunderstanding can be resolved.

What to practise next

Adapt a model to a different listener or situation. Keep the request, time reference and formal or informal address consistent.
